title: Concurrent Classification of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Occurrence From Routine Municipal Swimming‐Pool Monitoring Data: An Explainable Machine‐Learning Proof‐of‐Concept With Grouped Validation
content:
Machine-learning models classified Pseudomonas aeruginosa occurrence from routine swimming-pool monitoring data within the observed network, but performance fell in pools and facilities not used for training, and no model clearly outperformed residual chlorine alone. Previous-sample data gave no convincing early warning, so prospective multifacility validation is needed.


ABSTRACT

Routine swimming-pool surveillance may support detection-oriented screening, but rare positives and repeated sampling complicate model validation. This retrospective study analyzed 453 samples (37 occurrence-positive) from four chlorinated pools in two Greek facilities (2022–2025). Random forest, logistic regression, gradient boosting, and extra trees were evaluated using concurrent monitoring variables, physicochemical predictors and previous-sample information. Row-level, leave-one-pool-out, leave-one-facility-out and temporal validation were compared with a residual-chlorine-only baseline. Full-monitoring random forest achieved PR-AUC 0.532 within the network, decreasing to 0.386 for held-out pools and 0.157 for a held-out facility; corresponding logistic-regression values were 0.525 and 0.326. Residual chlorine alone achieved PR-AUC 0.452, with no model significantly outperforming it. Previous-sample predictors provided no convincing early-warning signal. Screening thresholds yielded substantial false alerts. These results support exploratory concurrent classification, not prospective warning or deployment readiness, and highlight the need for independent multifacility validation. Machine-learning models classified Pseudomonas aeruginosa occurrence from routine swimming-pool monitoring data within the observed network, but performance fell in pools and facilities not used for training, and no model clearly outperformed residual chlorine alone. Previous-sample data gave no convincing early warning, so prospective multifacility validation is needed.
